question.text: The Investment Manager for the Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (a Category III AIF) must comply with certain registration requirements with SEBI. Which requirement is a mandatory organisational position under current SEBI (AIF) framework?

answer.text: Only a Chief Investment Officer (CIO) is mandatory; Compliance Officer is optional.
Both a Chief Investment Officer and a Compliance Officer are mandatorily required.
Only a Compliance Officer is mandatory; CIO is optional.
Neither role is mandated; the sponsor decides based on fund size.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Investment Manager of an AIF is required to have both a Chief Investment Officer (CIO) — who must have adequate experience in financial services, investment planning, portfolio management — and a Compliance Officer to ensure SEBI compliance. Both are mandatory fit-and-proper positions under the AIF regulatory framework. The Trap: Options A, C, D drop one or both mandatory functions. The CIO-only trap plays on the common misconception that compliance is a back-office shared function that can be outsourced without a designated officer. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (Portfolio Managers) has a similar CIO + Compliance Officer + Principal Officer mandate. Compliance exams (III-A, III-C) test Compliance Officer designation rules. XIX-D tests the same for Cat I/II Managers. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a lean Cat III desk, the Compliance Officer often doubles as the AML Principal Officer — but the CIO must be distinct and must be on-site, fit-and-proper. Avoid 'CEO + CIO + Compliance Officer in one person' structures — SEBI inspections flag this as concentration risk and conflict of interest.
